label: Rank 6 CONFIRMED. The quality workflow hands new-file work back to the surface skill and names sk-code-skilled in parentheses, and the registry entry for that workflowMode declares forbidden Write, Edit and Task with mutatesWorkspace false. Both sides of the contradiction are now directly read lines, so the evidence grade moves from DERIVED to OBSERVED. The proposed replacement target .skilled/skills/sk-code/shared/references/workflow-implement.md exists, so the fix points at a real file.

Rank 7 CONFIRMED and sharpened. D4 usefulness at 25 points and D1 inter at 12 points are both unscored, so the saved PASS headline of 100/100 is normalized over 63 of 100 weighted points, with the single largest weight among the missing. The row's no-corpus sub-claim is true on disk at source.md line 12 and in the reports index, but rank 7 does not cite either line, so it is a citation defect rather than a factual one.

Rank 11 CONFIRMED and understated. The .opencode/specs/ key appears twice, in the CONDITIONAL tier table and again in the target-path checklist map, so replacing the map row alone leaves a live second entry; the first pass cited only the map. The directory is absent from disk and has zero tracked files, and git check-ignore reports only the negation pattern, so the absence is not a gitignored local directory. The replacement target is real: specs/ exists and the cited spec-folder checklist resolves.

Rank 13 CONFIRMED. The live run records an absolute machine-specific target root under the retired .opencode/skills/sk-code/code-quality path, the corpus and source columns both read not recorded, and the reports index states that rows are written by the benchmark harness at the moment it writes the report, which supports the row's claim that the harness owns the format and a decision is needed there.

Rank 14 CONFIRMED with a framing correction. In --all mode the checker calls the surface function with auto_rebuild=True and the switch defaults to on, while the per-file call uses the function's False default. The rebuild is deliberate by the function's own comment, so the fix must be a workflow sentence rather than a checker change. But quality's SKILL.md contains no --all mention at all and the tier row names the script bare, so the row supplies an absent instruction rather than correcting a wrong one; its readiness stands and its why should say absent, not wrong.

Second-model top five, in order: rank 3 name the CI surface, rank 4 report skipped checks as skipped, rank 7 behavior fixtures with D4 scoring, rank 11 replace the duplicated stale spec row, rank 6 hand back to the acting agent. Ranks 1, 2 and 5 leave the top five. Rank 1 drops because its false block is scoped to JavaScript and CSS and it is decision-gated; rank 2 drops because its evidence is DERIVED and the CI surface should declare first; rank 5 drops only because rank 6 evidence upgraded past it, and is the first divergence I would reverse.
